statement: Independently audited and kernel-checked final-theorem core: if 9/23<theta<1 satisfies the source short-prime input PI(theta), then every fixed 0<c<(1-theta)/3 gives, for all sufficiently large k and every 2k<n<=exp(c(log k)^2/loglog k), a prime divisor p in (k,k+3k^theta) of (n-k)...(n-1), hence p in (k,2k); theta=21/40 gives every c<19/120. The balanced four-range class has the exact theta window 9/23<theta<1. Post-promotion natural-proof extension, separately reconstructed by a same-model Codex auditor: adaptive upper thresholds and unbalanced lambda extend the same PI(theta)-conditional attaining theorem to every 0<theta<1, while the explicitly defined location-blind adaptive subdivided Konyagin little-o certificate class still cannot reach c>=(1-theta)/3. Its decisive logarithmic U/V/max selection algebra and strict-margin parameter feasibility are now kernel-checked for the full 0<theta<1 window, but the final adaptive ParametricRangeBuilder is not yet formalized. The enlarged barrier excludes prime-location-adaptive sparse covers, cross-block cancellation, stronger local prime input, and direct estimates of the true bad set. The BHP constant remains 19/120.

dependency_gaps: The abstract theta theorem assumes PI(theta); the theta=21/40 corollary imports the Baker--Harman--Pintz short-prime input exactly as the source paper does.

The complete four-range ParametricRangeBuilder and final conditional theorem are kernel-checked in Lean for 9/23<theta<1. For 0<theta<=9/23, Lean now checks exact adaptive parameter feasibility, V<=U, max-sandwich first-term budgets, the minimality lambda exponent, and an arbitrary-lambda r>=2 raw Konyagin interface. Remaining glue is the positive-real max-scale lift, least stopping-order construction, and uniform third/additive-term asymptotics; therefore no wider final divisor theorem is yet kernel-checked. The enlarged no-go remains natural-proof plus same-model cross-reconstruction rather than Lean or external review.

The enlarged no-go is confined to a location-blind deterministic-tail partition whose nonnegative Theorem 4.1 bounds are summed and required to be o(k^theta/log k). It does not cover sparse covers selected from actual prime locations, cross-block cancellation, stronger prime inputs, stronger exponential-sum estimates, or the true bad-set cardinality.
Novelty and publication priority remain unchecked.
